questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: That my study destination was an English-speaking country, that the university scored highly in various academic rankings, that the university offered different societies and other social initiatives that made is easier for visiting students to meet students from other countries and cultures, and that the university was located in a beautiful city, full of things to experience.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Relatively easy. The University of Edinburgh were great at communicating what to expect and where/how to find the information I needed.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Every visiting student were given a personal Visiting Student Advisor to communicate with and reach out to, if needed.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Very easy. I found my student accommodation through the University of Edinburgh's website. Even though it was off campus, it was only a 10 minute walk to classes from where I lived.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Most student accommodations in Edinburgh are located very close to campus. And those that are not, are typically located right by a bus stop or other forms of public transportation that takes you directly to campus within a very reasonable time frame.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The housing I lived in was not of the best quality in the world. It was quite old and you could hear a lot of noise from other people living in the building. But it had a great location, close to uni and a lovely park, and I met many great people in that building.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
The process was through OLA, where the host institution had to approve the courses I wanted to enroll in. 
There was also a matriculation process, where I needed to upload various documents to prove my arrival, and that I had been successfully enrolled in three courses, equivalent to 30 ETCS.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The visiting students office.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: When I registered for courses before coming to Edinburgh, I was only succesfull in enrolling in one of the three I wanted. But after the semester had begun it was a lot easier to register for other courses, and I ended up with the ones I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you don't get the classes/courses you want before starting the semester, fear not :) It is very easy to apply for other options, once you are there, and the course registration is open two weeks into the semester. Almost everyone I met, ended up with at least one og two other courses than they originally registered for.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I was only able to take 1st of 2nd year courses, and not 3rd year courses, even though I was in my 3rd year. But is was okay, because the courses I had were still very interesting and I did not experience that the academic level was beneath what I was used to from UCPH.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I felt that the teaching style at Edinburgh Uni was a more captivating and involving.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Contemporary Cinema
Visualising Scotland
Music 1A: Psychology of Music

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Visualising Scotland. I registered to this course later than the others, but it ended up being the course I enjoyed the most. Our professor was very competent and captivating in his way of teaching, and the course offered an exciting insight into Scottish culture and history that I did not know beforehand. When you spend an entire semester in Scotland, it feels important to know about its culture, and this course provided that information in an instructive and captivating way.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Train tickets for day trips. But if you buy a Railcard you save a lot of money.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Coffee was a lot less expensive than Copenhagen prices. Rent was more expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I joined different societies, e.g. The Film Society (FilmSoc), and the Scandinavian Society.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The societies and the welcome events in week 1.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go on as many little trips as possible. Scotland is full of beautiful little cities that are easy to get to by train :) The Highlands, the grand and beautiful nature up north, is also a big and very recommendable experience.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy I would say. People were very friendly and openminded.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: That the cars drive in the opposite side of the road - watch out, when you cross the street!

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: That people were so friendly, openminded and hospitable. The lady in the bakery would call you "love", which was such a nice gesture :)

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Make use of all the different societies that Edi Uni has to offer 
2. Go to your classes - the semester is quite short, and the assignments were a lot easier to write in those classes I had attended the most. 
3. Choose a living situation, where you live with other young people. It's a great way to meet new friends.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The lovely people that I met.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: When I missed my family and friends from back home.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
